text: INTRODUCING REBOLT ↓ PDF Introducing Rebolt The software platform for AI-powered operations 1 The Problem 2 What Changed 3 The Platform The Problem Operations don't live in one system Core operations are fragmented across ERP, CRM, spreadsheets, documents, email, and the knowledge of experienced employees. Existing systems record pieces of the business, but they rarely execute the company-specific process end to end. Teams compensate with: Manual handoffs between systems and teams Duplicate data entry and custom spreadsheets Informal workarounds that live in people's heads Who has this issue? Operations leaders whose critical processes—quoting, scheduling, billing, exception handling—cross multiple systems and depend on manual coordination; and IT teams asked to automate those processes without losing control over permissions, data access, and auditability. What is this costing? Long cycle times, high manual touch rates, errors that leak revenue, delayed invoicing, and forecasts built on stale data. The cost shows up in the P&L: margin, working capital, and throughput. What Changed AI can now execute the business, not just analyze it AI makes it possible to turn a company's operating knowledge into real software—not only to analyze the business, but to execute it. The data, rules, and know-how that used to be trapped in systems and people's heads can now be captured in a live operating model and expressed as governed software that runs the process. Why don't existing approaches work? Packaged SaaS forces the company to bend its process to fit the tool Data platforms make context usable but don't execute the operation Custom builds take years and go stale as the process changes The gap is execution: software that runs the company-specific process end to end, under governance, and evolves with it. The Platform How does Rebolt work? Holocron creates a live model of the company's data, processes, rules, permissions, and know-how. Rebolt's Software Factory turns that model into governed software and agents. The platform then runs those processes across the systems the company already uses. → Model: Holocron connects the objects your business runs on—customers, orders, projects, contracts—with the rules and permissions that govern them. → Generate: the Software Factory expresses that model as the applications, agents, and workflows each process requires. → Execute: Rebolt coordinates events, approvals, exceptions, and write-backs across your existing systems—governed, tested, and auditable. Where's the value? Start with one critical operation. Reduce manual handoffs, shorten cycle time, control exceptions, and connect execution to a measurable business outcome. Expand from there on the same operating model. Because every application, agent, and workflow is generated from one shared model, each new operation builds on the last instead of adding another disconnected tool.

PITCH REBOLT ↓ PDF Pitch Rebolt You see how Rebolt can run one of your critical operations. Here's how to help everyone on the team see it too 1 The Value 2 Getting Started 3 Common Concerns The Value What is Rebolt? Rebolt gives your company a governed operational software layer without a multi-year transformation program. It captures how a process actually works—the data, rules, permissions, and know-how—and turns it into governed software that executes the process across the systems you already use. Why would we want this? Your critical operations cross ERP, CRM, spreadsheets, email, and people's heads. Today that gap is closed by manual handoffs and duplicate entry—which slows cycle time, creates exceptions, and leaks revenue. The usual options don't close it: Packaged SaaS forces your process to bend to the tool Custom transformation programs take years and go stale Doing nothing keeps the cost buried in manual work and errors Who owns it? Owned by operations. Governed by IT. Executed by software. Operations teams evolve their processes directly, while IT keeps control of permissions, data access, testing, releases, and audit history. Getting Started We don't know where to start Think about the task you or your team dread doing every week. We begin with a workflow that's spreadsheet-heavy, touches several departments or approvals, relies on manual work, or uses multiple solutions stitched together. What are the steps to get started? Choose one critical operation—the process with the most manual handoffs, approvals, and exceptions Map the process: triggers, systems and business objects involved, rules, approvals, and what gets written back Define the operational metric that should improve: cycle time, manual touches, exception rate, or invoice accuracy Kickoff a pilot with Rebolt. Read: how to pilot Examples of operations Rebolt has run, by department Operations Project tracking dashboards that consolidate updates from multiple spreadsheets and departments. Approval workflows (purchase orders, vendor onboarding, expense approvals) replacing long email chains. Customer or partner portals to share project progress, documents, or metrics. Finance & Admin Expense reimbursement or invoice tracking apps instead of scattered Excel sheets and email threads. Budget vs. actuals dashboards pulling data from accounting tools like QuickBooks or NetSuite Contract renewal reminders connected to Google Drive or DocuSign CFO dashboarding for cashflow and accounting tracking Internal ticketing system to request product features, improving team collaboration 👩💻 HR & People Ops Employee onboarding/offboarding trackers pulling data from HRIS, Slack, and IT Time-off requests and approvals that integrate with calendars and payroll Parking slot and office spot manager app 📊 Sales & Customer Success Pipeline dashboards for quota and commission tracking pulling data from CRM Client implementation trackers that assign tasks and sync with CRM Customer onboarding app, avoiding manual forms or email chains Common Concerns We don't have time right now You might feel you don't have the time, but that's exactly why you need this. The truth is, your team is already losing time every day to manual, repetitive tasks that shouldn't exist. Every delay, every follow-up, every small thing that "just takes a few minutes" adds up to hours, days, and even weeks of lost productivity. When you automate, you don't find more time: you create it. What takes hours today can run on its own tomorrow. What slows you down now becomes instant. The companies that move fastest aren't the ones with more time. They're the ones that stop wasting it. You don't need extra time to start. You start and you'll get time. When piloting, Rebolt team will setup everything that's needed for the team to start using the tools. This is not the priority. Our current processes "work fine" Your team may think their current workflow "works fine", the reality is that it's slow, repetitive and bloated. If you dig into it, they go back and forth from Excel, emails, getting blocked by each other by simple requests waiting and excusing themselves "because they need to wait for X person". If one replies in 30 seconds what usually takes a day gets done in hours. What takes hours gets done now. What is automated is done x100 times a day what took weeks to do only once. Speed and automation compound. You will likely uncover deep inefficiencies and processes that might even be completely automated. Top companies already leverage AI to automate every part of the company possible, driving up to x10 improvements in productivity. Integrating AI into your company might not be the direct priority, but evolving your way of working to surpass your competitors is.

PILOT GUIDE (3 mins) ↓ PDF How to pilot Rebolt Introduce Rebolt to your team 1 Introduction 2 The pilot process 3 Unlock the full potential Introduction Once you've built internal awareness about Rebolt, it's time to get teams started. Pilots typically involve one or two teams and last four to six weeks. Participating in a pilot is an opportunity to see how Rebolt enables everyone to solve problems in a fraction of the time and effort, including work they may not have been qualified to handle before. Below, we explain how to select the best teams for the pilot and gather evidence to present a data-backed case for Rebolt. People define "pilot success" as users identifying Rebolt as a tool they enjoy using, which significantly improves their productivity in terms of both time and effort. The pilot process 1. Pick the teams or projects you want to pilot Rebolt List teams eager to try something new, with influence in the organization. Identify the groups on the list that spend significant time: Performing repetitive tasks at the computer Using Excel, Power BI, CRMs, Retool, Tableau, SAP, or any specific software. They will be the most likely to be sensitive to friction in their existing process and enthusiastic about a tool that eliminates their biggest pain points and enables new work that was impossible to do before. Once you have one or two teams in mind, approach them with a proposal with a use case, someone accountable and a timeline. Ask for modifications based on their input. 2. Create a "before Rebolt" survey The purpose is to gather the end user's impressions of the current state of the problem, to gauge how well (or not) it is working for them. Focus on obstacles with the current tooling. Below are sample topics. Adapt them at will. For inspiration, search Slack, Teams and Email looking for the keyword "Rebolt" Inspiration Survey How much time are you spending on this task? How many people know how to do the task? Is there any "know-it-all" who is responsible? On a scale of 1-5, how easy is the task in place? On a scale of 1-5, how time-consuming was the task in place? On a scale of 1-5, how do you enjoy the task in place? 3. Connect your tools to Rebolt Connecting your company tools is essential to experience the value. You might need to request IT keys and permissions. Contact Rebolt's team to help (if needed). Here are the essential ones: File storage: OneDrive/Google Drive/Dropbox Email: Outlook/Gmail Communication: Slack/Teams CRMs: HubSpot, Pipedrive, Attio Databases: PostgreSQL, MySQL, Access, BigQuery, Snowflake 4. Send a post-pilot survey Reformat the survey questions from step 2. Leave open text fields next to each question to collect extra details. Collect this feedback by a specific date, at least a week before meeting with leadership. 5. Compile data and present the case Most individuals love Rebolt, but leaders rarely have time to go through lists of anecdotes. Pull out the 4-5 most telling quantitative pieces of evidence and put them side-by-side with your baseline, adding an impactful quote to underscore the value of each metric. "We found 120% more work completed daily at the end of the pilot." Unlock the full potential A full onboarding is the next step. Learn how to leverage the most out of Rebolt in our onboarding guide.
